name: Japan

income_tax.summary: National income tax runs 5% to 45% (seven brackets) plus a 2.1% surtax on the tax and a flat 10% inhabitant tax, giving a combined top marginal rate of about 55.9%. Employees pay about 14.7% in social insurance (health 4.925%, child support 0.115%, welfare pension 9.15%, unemployment 0.5%), each with its own ceiling; the self-employed use National Pension (flat JPY 17,920 a month) and National Health Insurance. The basic deduction is JPY 620,000 for total income of JPY 6.55m to 23.5m (JPY 1.04m below JPY 4.89m, JPY 670,000 up to JPY 6.55m).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: National Pension is a flat JPY 17,920 a month in fiscal 2026 (JPY 215,040 a year; re-read on the Japan Pension Service page). National Health Insurance premiums are set by municipality (income-based plus per-capita parts) and no Tokyo ward rate table could be opened (several ward pages returned 404), so the self-employed rate here is a PLACEHOLDER equal to the employee rate, not a verified figure.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Combined rate = national rate x 1.021 (2.1% surtax) + 10% inhabitant tax (flat, charged on the prior year's income, not deductible). Per-capita inhabitant tax JPY 5,000 and forest tax JPY 1,000 not included. personal_allowance is the national basic deduction of JPY 620,000 that applies to total income between JPY 6.55m and 23.5m (PwC deductions page, 2026 and 2027); it is higher (JPY 670,000 to JPY 1.04m) below JPY 6.55m, and the inhabitant-tax basic deduction is JPY 430,000. The employment income deduction (JPY 740,000 minimum, up to JPY 1.95m above JPY 8.5m of salary; employees only) and the blue-return and social-insurance deductions are not included. Employee social insurance: health 4.925% to JPY 1.39m/month, welfare pension 9.15% to JPY 650,000/month; the 14.69% total is therefore not applied uniformly above those ceilings and no single cap is recorded. Long-term care 0.81% from age 40 is extra.

sources.title: Japan Pension Service - National Pension contributions

open_questions: National Health Insurance rates and caps for a Tokyo ward not found; the self-employed rate is a placeholder equal to the employee rate (confidence low for that figure).
Employee social insurance has per-component ceilings (pension JPY 650,000/month, health JPY 1.39m/month) that cannot be expressed as one cap.
The lower-income basic deduction tiers are not modelled.

employment_deduction.note: Employment income deduction (2026): JPY 740,000 minimum; 30% + JPY 80,000 up to JPY 3.6M of pay; 20% + JPY 440,000 to 6.6M; 10% + JPY 1.1M to 8.5M; JPY 1.95M above, expressed as marginal steps.

open_questions: Ministry of Foreign Affairs page returned HTTP 403; requirements taken from a secondary guide.

Whether a six-month stay creates Japanese tax residence (jusho/one-year kyosho test, see PwC residence page) and whether foreign income is taxable was not settled; social_security_applies=false is an inference (no residence card, no health insurance enrolment) and unverified.
regimes.name: Digital nomad visa (Designated Activities), from 2024
regimes.description: Six-month stay for remote workers earning at least JPY 10m a year from foreign sources, with private insurance covering at least JPY 10m of medical treatment. Limited to nationals of countries and regions with both a visa-exemption arrangement and a tax convention with Japan; no residence card is issued and the status cannot be extended.
regimes.duration_note: Six months; extension not allowed, new application only after six months outside Japan.

sources.title: Japan digital nomad visa: requirements and US tax rules

open_questions: Remittance-basis treatment of foreign-source income not verified on an opened page; treatment is recorded as standard because no share could be quantified.
regimes.name: Non-permanent resident taxpayer status
regimes.description: A resident foreign national with an aggregate stay of five years or less in the preceding ten years is a non-permanent resident (PwC residence page). Per the Japan jurisdiction research in this repository, foreign-source income is taxed only to the extent paid in or remitted to Japan (not confirmed on an opened page). It does not cover a remote worker's pay for work done in Japan: PwC states that Japan-source employment income is remuneration earned for services rendered in Japan, regardless of where or when it is paid.
regimes.duration_note: Status lasts while aggregate stay is five years or less in the preceding ten.

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Average 1LDK rent in Chiyoda, Chuo, Minato, Shinjuku and Shibuya, author's calculation from E-Housing ward data, article dated 18 March 2026. Numbeo city-centre 1-bedroom average JPY 202,375 (14 Oct 2026).

residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: the digital nomad status is only for nationals of countries with both visa exemption and a tax convention (the US qualifies per the source); stay is six months, non-extendable. Skilled employees need a work visa sponsored by an employer; the specific categories (Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Highly Skilled Professional points) were not verified from opened official pages.
